app/src/entry.node-server.ts:1-16 — createQwikCity from @builder.io/qwik-city/middleware/node: exactly mirrors the official node-server adapter entry
app/package.json:14-15 — pinned to @builder.io/qwik ^1.20.3, the current stable release (npm latest, published 2026-10-25), not the 2.0.0-rc.4 line
reach.rationale: The app reaches only for long-stable Qwik/Qwik City APIs and pins the current stable 1.20.x line rather than the Qwik 2.0 RC; no experimental or preview APIs appear in app source.

evidence: app/src (grep for 'experimental|unstable|preview|beta|alpha') — zero matches in any source file
app/src/lib/api.ts:36 — plain global fetch with a hand-rolled Map cache and concurrency limiter; no experimental framework features

justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so there are no unjustified reaches; every API used is the framework's documented default for the job it does.

findings.issue: undici ^7.0.0 is listed as a devDependency but is never imported by any app source file; the undici/Headers/Request/Response/FormData symbols seen in static analysis come from the framework's compiled middleware bundles, not app code.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused undici devDependency (Node's built-in fetch suffices), or document why it's needed.

findings.issue: Build artifacts (app/server/, app/dist/) are committed/present in the app tree; the single measured 'experimental' marker is a QRL serialization error string inside a compiled framework bundle, which can mislead tooling and reviews.
findings.suggestion: Ignore generated build output (server/, dist/) via app-level .gitignore and exclude it from analysis; judge only src/, adapters/ and config.

summary: This app is aggressively conservative on experimental surface area: it uses only Qwik/Qwik City APIs that have been stable since 1.0 and are still current in the docs, pinned to the current stable release (1.20.3) rather than the in-flight 2.0.0-rc line. The one measured 'experimental' marker and all exotic-looking imports (undici, node:http2, node:stream/web, crypto) come from compiled framework bundles in the build output, not from app source. Risk of breaking-change exposure is essentially zero; the only nit is an unused undici devDependency and committed build artifacts.
